paragraphs.text: And it came to pass soon afterwards, that he went about through cities and villages, preaching and bringing the good tidings of the kingdom of God, and with him the twelve,
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ καθεξῆς καὶ αὐτὸς διώδευεν κατὰ πόλιν καὶ κώμην κηρύσσων καὶ εὐαγγελιζόμενος τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ οἱ δώδεκα σὺν αὐτῷ,
paragraphs.translit: Kai egeneto en tō kathexēs kai autos diōdeuen kata polin kai kōmēn kēryssōn kai euangelizomenos tēn basileian tou theou, kai hoi dōdeka syn autō,

paragraphs.text: and certain women who had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities: Mary that was called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out,
paragraphs.original: καὶ γυναῖκές τινες αἳ ἦσαν τεθεραπευμέναι ἀπὸ πνευμάτων πονηρῶν καὶ ἀσθενειῶν, Μαρία ἡ καλουμένη Μαγδαληνή, ἀφʼ ἧς δαιμόνια ἑπτὰ ἐξεληλύθει,
paragraphs.translit: kai gynaikes tines hai ēsan tetherapeumenai apo pneumatōn ponērōn kai astheneiōn, Maria hē kaloumenē Magdalēnē, aphʼ hēs daimonia hepta exelēlythei,

paragraphs.text: and Joanna the wife of Chuzas Herod`s steward, and Susanna, and many others, who ministered unto them of their substance.
paragraphs.original: καὶ Ἰωάννα γυνὴ Χουζᾶ ἐπιτρόπου Ἡρῴδου καὶ Σουσάννα καὶ ἕτεραι πολλαί, αἵτινες διηκόνουν αὐτοῖς ἐκ τῶν ὑπαρχόντων αὐταῖς.
paragraphs.translit: kai Iōanna gynē Chouza epitropou Hērōdou kai Sousanna kai heterai pollai, haitines diēkonoun autois ek tōn hyparchontōn autais.

paragraphs.text: And when a great multitude came together, and they of every city resorted unto him, he spake by a parable:
paragraphs.original: Συνιόντος δὲ ὄχλου πολλοῦ καὶ τῶν κατὰ πόλιν ἐπιπορευομένων πρὸς αὐτὸν εἶπεν διὰ παραβολῆς·
paragraphs.translit: Syniontos de ochlou pollou kai tōn kata polin epiporeuomenōn pros auton eipen dia parabolēs·

paragraphs.text: The sower went forth to sow his seed: and as he sowed, some fell by the way side; and it was trodden under foot, and the birds of the heaven devoured it.
paragraphs.original: Ἐξῆλθεν ὁ σπείρων τοῦ σπεῖραι τὸν σπόρον αὐτοῦ. καὶ ἐν τῷ σπείρειν αὐτὸν ὃ μὲν ἔπεσεν παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν, καὶ κατεπατήθη καὶ τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ κατέφαγεν αὐτό.
paragraphs.translit: Exēlthen ho speirōn tou speirai ton sporon autou. kai en tō speirein auton ho men epesen para tēn hodon, kai katepatēthē kai ta peteina tou ouranou katephagen auto.

paragraphs.text: And other fell on the rock; and as soon as it grew, it withered away, because it had no moisture.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἕτερον κατέπεσεν ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν, καὶ φυὲν ἐξηράνθη διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν ἰκμάδα.
paragraphs.translit: kai heteron katepesen epi tēn petran, kai phyen exēranthē dia to mē echein ikmada.

paragraphs.text: And other fell amidst the thorns; and the thorns grew with it, and choked it.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἕτερον ἔπεσεν ἐν μέσῳ τῶν ἀκανθῶν, καὶ συμφυεῖσαι αἱ ἄκανθαι ἀπέπνιξαν αὐτό.
paragraphs.translit: kai heteron epesen en mesō tōn akanthōn, kai symphyeisai hai akanthai apepnixan auto.

paragraphs.text: And other fell into the good ground, and grew, and brought forth fruit a hundredfold. As he said these things, he cried, He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἕτερον ἔπεσεν εἰς τὴν γῆν τὴν ἀγαθήν, καὶ φυὲν ἐποίησεν καρπὸν ἑκατονταπλασίονα. ταῦτα λέγων ἐφώνει· Ὁ ἔχων ὦτα ἀκούειν ἀκουέτω.
paragraphs.translit: kai heteron epesen eis tēn gēn tēn agathēn, kai phyen epoiēsen karpon hekatontaplasiona. tauta legōn ephōnei· Ho echōn ōta akouein akouetō.

paragraphs.text: And his disciples asked him what this parable might be.
paragraphs.original: Ἐπηρώτων δὲ αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ τίς αὕτη εἴη ἡ παραβολή.
paragraphs.translit: Epērōtōn de auton hoi mathētai autou tis hautē eiē hē parabolē.

paragraphs.text: And he said, Unto you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of God: but to the rest in parables; that seeing they may not see, and hearing they may not understand.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ὑμῖν δέδοται γνῶναι τὰ μυστήρια τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ θεοῦ, τοῖς δὲ λοιποῖς ἐν παραβολαῖς, ἵνα βλέποντες μὴ βλέπωσιν καὶ ἀκούοντες μὴ συνιῶσιν.
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen· Hymin dedotai gnōnai ta mystēria tēs basileias tou theou, tois de loipois en parabolais, hina blepontes mē blepōsin kai akouontes mē syniōsin.

paragraphs.text: Now the parable is this: The seed is the word of God.
paragraphs.original: Ἔστιν δὲ αὕτη ἡ παραβολή· Ὁ σπόρος ἐστὶν ὁ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Estin de hautē hē parabolē· Ho sporos estin ho logos tou theou.

paragraphs.text: And those by the way side are they that have heard; then cometh the devil, and taketh away the word from their heart, that they may not believe and be saved.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν εἰσιν οἱ ἀκούσαντες, εἶτα ἔρχεται ὁ διάβολος καὶ αἴρει τὸν λόγον ἀπὸ τῆς καρδίας αὐτῶν, ἵνα μὴ πιστεύσαντες σωθῶσιν.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de para tēn hodon eisin hoi akousantes, eita erchetai ho diabolos kai airei ton logon apo tēs kardias autōn, hina mē pisteusantes sōthōsin.

paragraphs.text: And those on the rock [are] they who, when they have heard, receive the word with joy; and these have no root, who for a while believe, and in time of temptation fall away.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ ἐπὶ τῆς πέτρας οἳ ὅταν ἀκούσωσιν μετὰ χαρᾶς δέχονται τὸν λόγον, καὶ οὗτοι ῥίζαν οὐκ ἔχουσιν, οἳ πρὸς καιρὸν πιστεύουσιν καὶ ἐν καιρῷ πειρασμοῦ ἀφίστανται.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de epi tēs petras hoi hotan akousōsin meta charas dechontai ton logon, kai houtoi rhizan ouk echousin, hoi pros kairon pisteuousin kai en kairō peirasmou aphistantai.

paragraphs.text: And that which fell among the thorns, these are they that have heard, and as they go on their way they are choked with cares and riches and pleasures of [this] life, and bring no fruit to perfection.
paragraphs.original: τὸ δὲ εἰς τὰς ἀκάνθας πεσόν, οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ ἀκούσαντες, καὶ ὑπὸ μεριμνῶν καὶ πλούτου καὶ ἡδονῶν τοῦ βίου πορευόμενοι συμπνίγονται καὶ οὐ τελεσφοροῦσιν.
paragraphs.translit: to de eis tas akanthas peson, houtoi eisin hoi akousantes, kai hypo merimnōn kai ploutou kai hēdonōn tou biou poreuomenoi sympnigontai kai ou telesphorousin.

paragraphs.text: And that in the good ground, these are such as in an honest and good heart, having heard the word, hold it fast, and bring forth fruit with patience.
paragraphs.original: τὸ δὲ ἐν τῇ καλῇ γῇ, οὗτοί εἰσιν οἵτινες ἐν καρδίᾳ καλῇ καὶ ἀγαθῇ ἀκούσαντες τὸν λόγον κατέχουσιν καὶ καρποφοροῦσιν ἐν ὑπομονῇ.
paragraphs.translit: to de en tē kalē gē, houtoi eisin hoitines en kardia kalē kai agathē akousantes ton logon katechousin kai karpophorousin en hypomonē.

paragraphs.text: And no man, when he hath lighted a lamp, covereth it with a vessel, or putteth it under a bed; but putteth it on a stand, that they that enter in may see the light.
paragraphs.original: Οὐδεὶς δὲ λύχνον ἅψας καλύπτει αὐτὸν σκεύει ἢ ὑποκάτω κλίνης τίθησιν, ἀλλʼ ἐπὶ λυχνίας τίθησιν, ἵνα οἱ εἰσπορευόμενοι βλέπωσιν τὸ φῶς.
paragraphs.translit: Oudeis de lychnon hapsas kalyptei auton skeuei ē hypokatō klinēs tithēsin, allʼ epi lychnias tithēsin, hina hoi eisporeuomenoi blepōsin to phōs.

paragraphs.text: For nothing is hid, that shall not be made manifest; nor [anything] secret, that shall not be known and come to light.
paragraphs.original: οὐ γάρ ἐστιν κρυπτὸν ὃ οὐ φανερὸν γενήσεται, οὐδὲ ἀπόκρυφον ὃ οὐ μὴ γνωσθῇ καὶ εἰς φανερὸν ἔλθῃ.
paragraphs.translit: ou gar estin krypton ho ou phaneron genēsetai, oude apokryphon ho ou mē gnōsthē kai eis phaneron elthē.

paragraphs.text: Take heed therefore how ye hear: for whosoever hath, to him shall be given; and whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken away even that which he thinketh he hath.
paragraphs.original: βλέπετε οὖν πῶς ἀκούετε· ὃς ἂν γὰρ ἔχῃ, δοθήσεται αὐτῷ, καὶ ὃς ἂν μὴ ἔχῃ, καὶ ὃ δοκεῖ ἔχειν ἀρθήσεται ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: blepete oun pōs akouete· hos an gar echē, dothēsetai autō, kai hos an mē echē, kai ho dokei echein arthēsetai apʼ autou.

paragraphs.text: And there came to him his mother and brethren, and they could not come at him for the crowd.
paragraphs.original: Παρεγένετο δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν ἡ μήτηρ καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ οὐκ ἠδύναντο συντυχεῖν αὐτῷ διὰ τὸν ὄχλον.
paragraphs.translit: Paregeneto de pros auton hē mētēr kai hoi adelphoi autou, kai ouk ēdynanto syntychein autō dia ton ochlon.

paragraphs.text: And it was told him, Thy mother and thy brethren stand without, desiring to see thee.
paragraphs.original: ἀπηγγέλη δὲ αὐτῷ· Ἡ μήτηρ σου καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοί σου ἑστήκασιν ἔξω ἰδεῖν σε θέλοντες.
paragraphs.translit: apēngelē de autō· Hē mētēr sou kai hoi adelphoi sou hestēkasin exō idein se thelontes.

paragraphs.text: But he answered and said unto them, My mother and my brethren are these that hear the word of God, and do it.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Μήτηρ μου καὶ ἀδελφοί μου οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ ἀκούοντες καὶ ποιοῦντες.
paragraphs.translit: ho de apokritheis eipen pros autous· Mētēr mou kai adelphoi mou houtoi eisin hoi ton logon tou theou akouontes kai poiountes.

paragraphs.text: Now it came to pass on one of those days, that he entered into a boat, himself and his disciples; and he said unto them, Let us go over unto the other side of the lake: and they launched forth.
paragraphs.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν μιᾷ τῶν ἡμερῶν καὶ αὐτὸς ἐνέβη εἰς πλοῖον καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Διέλθωμεν εἰς τὸ πέραν τῆς λίμνης, καὶ ἀνήχθησαν.
paragraphs.translit: Egeneto de en mia tōn hēmerōn kai autos enebē eis ploion kai hoi mathētai autou, kai eipen pros autous· Dielthōmen eis to peran tēs limnēs, kai anēchthēsan.

paragraphs.text: But as they sailed he fell asleep: and there came down a storm of wind on the lake; and they were filling [with water], and were in jeopardy.
paragraphs.original: πλεόντων δὲ αὐτῶν ἀφύπνωσεν. καὶ κατέβη λαῖλαψ ἀνέμου εἰς τὴν λίμνην, καὶ συνεπληροῦντο καὶ ἐκινδύνευον.
paragraphs.translit: pleontōn de autōn aphypnōsen. kai katebē lailaps anemou eis tēn limnēn, kai syneplērounto kai ekindyneuon.

paragraphs.text: And they came to him, and awoke him, saying, Master, master, we perish. And he awoke, and rebuked the wind and the raging of the water: and they ceased, and there was a calm.
paragraphs.original: προσελθόντες δὲ διήγειραν αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Ἐπιστάτα ἐπιστάτα, ἀπολλύμεθα· ὁ δὲ διεγερθεὶς ἐπετίμησεν τῷ ἀνέμῳ καὶ τῷ κλύδωνι τοῦ ὕδατος, καὶ ἐπαύσαντο, καὶ ἐγένετο γαλήνη.
paragraphs.translit: proselthontes de diēgeiran auton legontes· Epistata epistata, apollymetha· ho de diegertheis epetimēsen tō anemō kai tō klydōni tou hydatos, kai epausanto, kai egeneto galēnē.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them, Where is your faith? And being afraid they marvelled, saying one to another, Who then is this, that he commandeth even the winds and the water, and they obey him?
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς· Ποῦ ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν; φοβηθέντες δὲ ἐθαύμασαν, λέγοντες πρὸς ἀλλήλους· Τίς ἄρα οὗτός ἐστιν ὅτι καὶ τοῖς ἀνέμοις ἐπιτάσσει καὶ τῷ ὕδατι, καὶ ὑπακούουσιν αὐτῷ;
paragraphs.translit: eipen de autois· Pou hē pistis hymōn; phobēthentes de ethaumasan, legontes pros allēlous· Tis ara houtos estin hoti kai tois anemois epitassei kai tō hydati, kai hypakouousin autō;

paragraphs.text: And they arrived at the country of the Gerasenes, which is over against Galilee.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ κατέπλευσαν εἰς τὴν χώραν τῶν Γερασηνῶν, ἥτις ἐστὶν ἀντιπέρα τῆς Γαλιλαίας.
paragraphs.translit: Kai katepleusan eis tēn chōran tōn Gerasēnōn, hētis estin antipera tēs Galilaias.

paragraphs.text: And when he was come forth upon the land, there met him a certain man out of the city, who had demons; and for a long time he had worn no clothes, and abode not in [any] house, but in the tombs.
paragraphs.original: ἐξελθόντι δὲ αὐτῷ ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ὑπήντησεν ἀνήρ τις ἐκ τῆς πόλεως ἔχων δαιμόνια· καὶ χρόνῳ ἱκανῷ οὐκ ἐνεδύσατο ἱμάτιον, καὶ ἐν οἰκίᾳ οὐκ ἔμενεν ἀλλʼ ἐν τοῖς μνήμασιν.
paragraphs.translit: exelthonti de autō epi tēn gēn hypēntēsen anēr tis ek tēs poleōs echōn daimonia· kai chronō hikanō ouk enedysato himation, kai en oikia ouk emenen allʼ en tois mnēmasin.

paragraphs.text: And when he saw Jesus, he cried out, and fell down before him, and with a loud voice said, What have I to do with thee, Jesus, thou Son of the Most High God? I beseech thee, torment me not.
paragraphs.original: ἰδὼν δὲ τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀνακράξας προσέπεσεν αὐτῷ καὶ φωνῇ μεγάλῃ εἶπεν· Τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί, Ἰησοῦ υἱὲ τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ὑψίστου; δέομαί σου, μή με βασανίσῃς·
paragraphs.translit: idōn de ton Iēsoun anakraxas prosepesen autō kai phōnē megalē eipen· Ti emoi kai soi, Iēsou hyie tou theou tou hypsistou; deomai sou, mē me basanisēs·

paragraphs.text: For he was commanding the unclean spirit to come out from the man. For oftentimes it had seized him: and he was kept under guard, and bound with chains and fetters; and breaking the bands asunder, he was driven of the demon into the deserts.
paragraphs.original: παρήγγελλεν γὰρ τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἀκαθάρτῳ ἐξελθεῖν ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου. πολλοῖς γὰρ χρόνοις συνηρπάκει αὐτόν, καὶ ἐδεσμεύετο ἁλύσεσιν καὶ πέδαις φυλασσόμενος, καὶ διαρρήσσων τὰ δεσμὰ ἠλαύνετο ὑπὸ τοῦ δαιμονίου εἰς τὰς ἐρήμους.
paragraphs.translit: parēngellen gar tō pneumati tō akathartō exelthein apo tou anthrōpou. pollois gar chronois synērpakei auton, kai edesmeueto halysesin kai pedais phylassomenos, kai diarrēssōn ta desma ēlauneto hypo tou daimoniou eis tas erēmous.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus asked him, What is thy name? And he said, Legion; for many demons were entered into him.
paragraphs.original: ἐπηρώτησεν δὲ αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Τί σοι ὄνομά ἐστιν; ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Λεγιών, ὅτι εἰσῆλθεν δαιμόνια πολλὰ εἰς αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: epērōtēsen de auton ho Iēsous· Ti soi onoma estin; ho de eipen· Legiōn, hoti eisēlthen daimonia polla eis auton.

paragraphs.text: And they entreated him that he would not command them to depart into the abyss.
paragraphs.original: καὶ παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν ἵνα μὴ ἐπιτάξῃ αὐτοῖς εἰς τὴν ἄβυσσον ἀπελθεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: kai parekaloun auton hina mē epitaxē autois eis tēn abysson apelthein.

paragraphs.text: Now there was there a herd of many swine feeding on the mountain: and they entreated him that he would give them leave to enter into them. And he gave them leave.
paragraphs.original: Ἦν δὲ ἐκεῖ ἀγέλη χοίρων ἱκανῶν βοσκομένη ἐν τῷ ὄρει· καὶ παρεκάλεσαν αὐτὸν ἵνα ἐπιτρέψῃ αὐτοῖς εἰς ἐκείνους εἰσελθεῖν· καὶ ἐπέτρεψεν αὐτοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: Ēn de ekei agelē choirōn hikanōn boskomenē en tō orei· kai parekalesan auton hina epitrepsē autois eis ekeinous eiselthein· kai epetrepsen autois.

paragraphs.text: And the demons came out from the man, and entered into the swine: and the herd rushed down the steep into the lake, and were drowned.
paragraphs.original: ἐξελθόντα δὲ τὰ δαιμόνια ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου εἰσῆλθον εἰς τοὺς χοίρους, καὶ ὥρμησεν ἡ ἀγέλη κατὰ τοῦ κρημνοῦ εἰς τὴν λίμνην καὶ ἀπεπνίγη.
paragraphs.translit: exelthonta de ta daimonia apo tou anthrōpou eisēlthon eis tous choirous, kai hōrmēsen hē agelē kata tou krēmnou eis tēn limnēn kai apepnigē.

paragraphs.text: And when they that fed them saw what had come to pass, they fled, and told it in the city and in the country.
paragraphs.original: Ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ βόσκοντες τὸ γεγονὸς ἔφυγον καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν εἰς τὴν πόλιν καὶ εἰς τοὺς ἀγρούς.
paragraphs.translit: Idontes de hoi boskontes to gegonos ephygon kai apēngeilan eis tēn polin kai eis tous agrous.

paragraphs.text: And they went out to see what had come to pass; and they came to Jesus, and found the man, from whom the demons were gone out, sitting, clothed and in his right mind, at the feet of Jesus: and they were afraid.
paragraphs.original: ἐξῆλθον δὲ ἰδεῖν τὸ γεγονὸς καὶ ἦλθον πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν, καὶ εὗρον καθήμενον τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἀφʼ οὗ τὰ δαιμόνια ἐξῆλθεν ἱματισμένον καὶ σωφρονοῦντα παρὰ τοὺς πόδας τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν.
paragraphs.translit: exēlthon de idein to gegonos kai ēlthon pros ton Iēsoun, kai heuron kathēmenon ton anthrōpon aphʼ hou ta daimonia exēlthen himatismenon kai sōphronounta para tous podas tou Iēsou, kai ephobēthēsan.

paragraphs.text: And they that saw it told them how he that was possessed with demons was made whole.
paragraphs.original: ἀπήγγειλαν δὲ αὐτοῖς οἱ ἰδόντες πῶς ἐσώθη ὁ δαιμονισθείς.
paragraphs.translit: apēngeilan de autois hoi idontes pōs esōthē ho daimonistheis.

paragraphs.text: And all the people of the country of the Gerasenes round about asked him to depart from them, for they were holden with great fear: and he entered into a boat, and returned.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἠρώτησεν αὐτὸν ἅπαν τὸ πλῆθος τῆς περιχώρου τῶν Γερασηνῶν ἀπελθεῖν ἀπʼ αὐτῶν, ὅτι φόβῳ μεγάλῳ συνείχοντο· αὐτὸς δὲ ἐμβὰς εἰς πλοῖον ὑπέστρεψεν.
paragraphs.translit: kai ērōtēsen auton hapan to plēthos tēs perichōrou tōn Gerasēnōn apelthein apʼ autōn, hoti phobō megalō syneichonto· autos de embas eis ploion hypestrepsen.

paragraphs.text: But the man from whom the demons were gone out prayed him that he might be with him: but he sent him away, saying,
paragraphs.original: ἐδεῖτο δὲ αὐτοῦ ὁ ἀνὴρ ἀφʼ οὗ ἐξεληλύθει τὰ δαιμόνια εἶναι σὺν αὐτῷ· ἀπέλυσεν δὲ αὐτὸν λέγων·
paragraphs.translit: edeito de autou ho anēr aphʼ hou exelēlythei ta daimonia einai syn autō· apelysen de auton legōn·

paragraphs.text: Return to thy house, and declare how great things God hath done for thee. And he went his way, publishing throughout the whole city how great things Jesus had done for him.
paragraphs.original: Ὑπόστρεφε εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου, καὶ διηγοῦ ὅσα σοι ἐποίησεν ὁ θεός. καὶ ἀπῆλθεν καθʼ ὅλην τὴν πόλιν κηρύσσων ὅσα ἐποίησεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς.
paragraphs.translit: Hypostrephe eis ton oikon sou, kai diēgou hosa soi epoiēsen ho theos. kai apēlthen kathʼ holēn tēn polin kēryssōn hosa epoiēsen autō ho Iēsous.

paragraphs.text: And as Jesus returned, the multitude welcomed him; for they were all waiting for him.
paragraphs.original: Ἐν δὲ τῷ ὑποστρέφειν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀπεδέξατο αὐτὸν ὁ ὄχλος, ἦσαν γὰρ πάντες προσδοκῶντες αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: En de tō hypostrephein ton Iēsoun apedexato auton ho ochlos, ēsan gar pantes prosdokōntes auton.

paragraphs.text: And behold, there came a man named Jairus, and he was a ruler of the synagogue: and he fell down at Jesus` feet, and besought him to come into his house;
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἦλθεν ἀνὴρ ᾧ ὄνομα Ἰάϊρος, καὶ οὗτος ἄρχων τῆς συναγωγῆς ὑπῆρχεν, καὶ πεσὼν παρὰ τοὺς πόδας τοῦ Ἰησοῦ παρεκάλει αὐτὸν εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: kai idou ēlthen anēr hō onoma Iairos, kai houtos archōn tēs synagōgēs hypērchen, kai pesōn para tous podas tou Iēsou parekalei auton eiselthein eis ton oikon autou,

paragraphs.text: for he had an only daughter, about twelve years of age, and she was dying. But as he went the multitudes thronged him.
paragraphs.original: ὅτι θυγάτηρ μονογενὴς ἦν αὐτῷ ὡς ἐτῶν δώδεκα καὶ αὐτὴ ἀπέθνῃσκεν. Ἐν δὲ τῷ ὑπάγειν αὐτὸν οἱ ὄχλοι συνέπνιγον αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: hoti thygatēr monogenēs ēn autō hōs etōn dōdeka kai autē apethnēsken. En de tō hypagein auton hoi ochloi synepnigon auton.

paragraphs.text: And a woman having an issue of blood twelve years, who had spent all her living upon physicians, and could not be healed of any,
paragraphs.original: καὶ γυνὴ οὖσα ἐν ῥύσει αἵματος ἀπὸ ἐτῶν δώδεκα, ἥτις ἰατροῖς προσαναλώσασα ὅλον τὸν βίον οὐκ ἴσχυσεν ἀπʼ οὐδενὸς θεραπευθῆναι,
paragraphs.translit: kai gynē ousa en rhysei haimatos apo etōn dōdeka, hētis iatrois prosanalōsasa holon ton bion ouk ischysen apʼ oudenos therapeuthēnai,

paragraphs.text: came behind him, and touched the border of his garment: and immediately the issue of her blood stanched.
paragraphs.original: προσελθοῦσα ὄπισθεν ἥψατο τοῦ κρασπέδου τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ, καὶ παραχρῆμα ἔστη ἡ ῥύσις τοῦ αἵματος αὐτῆς.
paragraphs.translit: proselthousa opisthen hēpsato tou kraspedou tou himatiou autou, kai parachrēma estē hē rhysis tou haimatos autēs.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus said, Who is it that touched me? And when all denied, Peter said, and they that were with him, Master, the multitudes press thee and crush [thee].
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Τίς ὁ ἁψάμενός μου; ἀρνουμένων δὲ πάντων εἶπεν ὁ Πέτρος· Ἐπιστάτα, οἱ ὄχλοι συνέχουσίν σε καὶ ἀποθλίβουσιν.
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen ho Iēsous· Tis ho hapsamenos mou; arnoumenōn de pantōn eipen ho Petros· Epistata, hoi ochloi synechousin se kai apothlibousin.

paragraphs.text: But Jesus said, Some one did touch me; for I perceived that power had gone forth from me.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ἥψατό μού τις, ἐγὼ γὰρ ἔγνων δύναμιν ἐξεληλυθυῖαν ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Iēsous eipen· Hēpsato mou tis, egō gar egnōn dynamin exelēlythyian apʼ emou.

paragraphs.text: And when the woman saw that she was not hid, she came trembling, and falling down before him declared in the presence of all the people for what cause she touched him, and how she was healed immediately.
paragraphs.original: ἰδοῦσα δὲ ἡ γυνὴ ὅτι οὐκ ἔλαθεν τρέμουσα ἦλθεν καὶ προσπεσοῦσα αὐτῷ διʼ ἣν αἰτίαν ἥψατο αὐτοῦ ἀπήγγειλεν ἐνώπιον παντὸς τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ ὡς ἰάθη παραχρῆμα.
paragraphs.translit: idousa de hē gynē hoti ouk elathen tremousa ēlthen kai prospesousa autō diʼ hēn aitian hēpsato autou apēngeilen enōpion pantos tou laou kai hōs iathē parachrēma.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto her, Daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Θυγάτηρ, ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε· πορεύου εἰς εἰρήνην.
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen autē· Thygatēr, hē pistis sou sesōken se· poreuou eis eirēnēn.

paragraphs.text: While he yet spake, there cometh one from the ruler of the synagogue`s [house], saying, Thy daughter is dead; trouble not the Teacher.
paragraphs.original: Ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ἔρχεταί τις παρὰ τοῦ ἀρχισυναγώγου λέγων ὅτι Τέθνηκεν ἡ θυγάτηρ σου, μηκέτι σκύλλε τὸν διδάσκαλον.
paragraphs.translit: Eti autou lalountos erchetai tis para tou archisynagōgou legōn hoti Tethnēken hē thygatēr sou, mēketi skylle ton didaskalon.

paragraphs.text: But Jesus hearing it, answered him, Fear not: only believe, and she shall be made whole.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἀκούσας ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ· Μὴ φοβοῦ, μόνον πίστευσον, καὶ σωθήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Iēsous akousas apekrithē autō· Mē phobou, monon pisteuson, kai sōthēsetai.

paragraphs.text: And when he came to the house, he suffered not any man to enter in with him, save Peter, and John, and James, and the father of the maiden and her mother.
paragraphs.original: ἐλθὼν δὲ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν οὐκ ἀφῆκεν εἰσελθεῖν τινα σὺν αὐτῷ εἰ μὴ Πέτρον καὶ Ἰωάννην καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ τὸν πατέρα τῆς παιδὸς καὶ τὴν μητέρα.
paragraphs.translit: elthōn de eis tēn oikian ouk aphēken eiselthein tina syn autō ei mē Petron kai Iōannēn kai Iakōbon kai ton patera tēs paidos kai tēn mētera.

paragraphs.text: And all were weeping, and bewailing her: but he said, Weep not; for she is not dead, but sleepeth.
paragraphs.original: ἔκλαιον δὲ πάντες καὶ ἐκόπτοντο αὐτήν. ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Μὴ κλαίετε, οὐ γὰρ ἀπέθανεν ἀλλὰ καθεύδει.
paragraphs.translit: eklaion de pantes kai ekoptonto autēn. ho de eipen· Mē klaiete, ou gar apethanen alla katheudei.

paragraphs.text: And they laughed him to scorn, knowing that she was dead.
paragraphs.original: καὶ κατεγέλων αὐτοῦ, εἰδότες ὅτι ἀπέθανεν.
paragraphs.translit: kai kategelōn autou, eidotes hoti apethanen.

paragraphs.text: But he, taking her by the hand, called, saying, Maiden, arise.
paragraphs.original: αὐτὸς δὲ κρατήσας τῆς χειρὸς αὐτῆς ἐφώνησεν λέγων· Ἡ παῖς, ἔγειρε.
paragraphs.translit: autos de kratēsas tēs cheiros autēs ephōnēsen legōn· Hē pais, egeire.

paragraphs.text: And her spirit returned, and she rose up immediately: and he commanded that [something] be given her to eat.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐπέστρεψεν τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτῆς, καὶ ἀνέστη παραχρῆμα, καὶ διέταξεν αὐτῇ δοθῆναι φαγεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: kai epestrepsen to pneuma autēs, kai anestē parachrēma, kai dietaxen autē dothēnai phagein.

paragraphs.text: And her parents were amazed: but he charged them to tell no man what had been done.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐξέστησαν οἱ γονεῖς αὐτῆς· ὁ δὲ παρήγγειλεν αὐτοῖς μηδενὶ εἰπεῖν τὸ γεγονός.
paragraphs.translit: kai exestēsan hoi goneis autēs· ho de parēngeilen autois mēdeni eipein to gegonos.
